question.text: A particle moving in the x-y plane experiences a time-dependent acceleration described by a = (2t î + 3t² ĵ) m/s². At the moment t = 0, it begins moving from the origin with an initial velocity of 2 m/s directed along the positive x-axis. Determine the velocity vector and the position coordinates of the particle at t = 1 s.

solution.approach: Integrate the acceleration once for velocity, adding the initial velocity, then integrate again for position, starting from the origin.

steps.text: Integrate a with respect to time and add the initial velocity to get v(t).
Integrate v with respect to time, starting from the origin, to get the coordinates.
Substitute t = 1 s to get the coordinates.

common_mistakes.text: Integrating the acceleration for velocity without adding the initial velocity of 2 m/s along the x-axis gives v(1) = (î + ĵ) m/s instead of (3î + ĵ) m/s.
Integrating the acceleration components twice without carrying the initial velocity into the position integral gives an x-coordinate of 1/3 m instead of 7/3 m.
